wind bell.d: a decorative arrangement of pieces of metal or glass or pottery that hang together loosely so the wind can cause them to tinkle

wing commander.d: one who is next below a group captain

winter flowering cherry.d: shrub or tree native to Japan cultivated as an ornamental for its rose-pink flowers

wild fig.d: a strangler tree native to southern Florida and West Indies; begins as an epiphyte eventually developing many thick aerial roots and covering enormous areas

wire glass.d: a glass that contains a layer of wire netting in it

wild ginger.d: low-growing perennial herb with pungent gingery leaves and rhizomes

wild rye.d: any of several grasses of the genus Elymus

wing loading.d: the ratio of the weight of an airplane to its wing area

wind rose.d: weather map showing the frequency and strength of winds from different directions

window dressing.d: a showy misrepresentation intended to conceal something unpleasant

wind generation.d: power derived from the wind (as by windmills)

wishing cap.d: a magical cap that secures whatever one wishes for

wild lily of the valley.d: North American evergreen with small pinkish bell-shaped flowers and oblong leaves used formerly for shinplasters

wind instrument.d: a musical instrument in which the sound is produced by an enclosed column of air that is moved by the breath

wild pumpkin.d: perennial vine of dry parts of central and southwestern United States and Mexico having small hard mottled green inedible fruit

wild rice.d: grains of aquatic grass of North America

wild man.d: a person who is not socialized

window seat.d: a bench or similar seat built into a window recess

window lock.d: a lock attached to the sashes of a double hung window that can fix both in the shut position

wind off.d: reverse the winding or twisting of

wide screen.d: a projection screen that is much wider than it is high

wind sleeve.d: a truncated cloth cone mounted on a mast; used (e.g., at airports) to show the direction of the wind

wind gap.d: a pass in a mountain ridge with no stream flowing through it
